chapters.title: The Two Ways
chapters.html:
Psalms 1

1Blessed is the man
who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked,
nor stand in the way of sinners,
nor sit in the seat of scoffers;

2but his delight is in the law of the LORD,
and on His law he meditates day and night.

3He will be like a tree
planted by streams of water,
that yields its fruit in its season,
and its leaf does not wither;
in all that he does, he prospers.

4The wicked are not so,
but are like chaff that the wind drives away.

5Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment,
nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous;

6for the LORD knows the way of the righteous,
but the way of the wicked will perish.

Notes

  • The text of the Psalms — rendered from the Hebrew. The Ethiopian Psalter, like the Greek, has a hundred and fifty-one psalms; Psalm 151 is rendered from the Greek. Verse numbers follow the English: where the Hebrew counts a psalm's title as verse 1, the title stands above the psalm without a number, and the English verse 1 is the Hebrew verse 2.

  • v1 "Blessed is the man" — ashrei ha-ish, happy, how fortunate, the first word of the Psalter. Walking, standing and sitting: each line goes one step further into the company of the wicked.

  • v1 "scoffers" — letsim, those who mock what is good, the fools of Proverbs (Proverbs 1:22; 9:7–8).

  • v2 "the law of the LORD" — torat YHWH, the instruction of the LORD, the teaching given to Israel. Meditates is yehgeh, a low murmuring, reading half aloud (Joshua 1:8).

  • v3 "like a tree planted by streams of water" — Blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD… He is like a tree planted by water (Jeremiah 17:7–8). Planted is shatul, transplanted, set in place on purpose.

  • v4 "like chaff that the wind drives away" — the husks blown off the threshing floor (Job 21:18; Hosea 13:3).

  • v6 "the LORD knows the way of the righteous" — yodea, knows with care and favor (Nahum 1:7). The psalm opens with blessed and ends with perish: the two ways of Deuteronomy 30:15–20.

speech.text: Psalms 1
Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;
but his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on His law he meditates day and night.
He will be like a tree planted by streams of water, that yields its fruit in its season, and its leaf does not wither; in all that he does, he prospers.
The wicked are not so, but are like chaff that the wind drives away.
Therefore the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous;
for the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish.

chapters.title: You Are My Son
chapters.html:
Psalms 2

1Why do the nations rage,
and the peoples plot in vain?

2The kings of the earth take their stand,
and the rulers take counsel together,
against the LORD and against His anointed:

3"Let us burst their bonds apart
and cast their cords away from us."

4He who sits in the heavens laughs;
the Lord holds them in derision.

5Then He will speak to them in His anger
and terrify them in His fury:

6"As for Me, I have set My king
on Zion, My holy mountain."

7I will tell of the decree of the LORD.
He said to me, "You are My son;
today I have fathered you.

8Ask of Me, and I will make the nations your inheritance,
and the ends of the earth your possession.

9You will break them with a rod of iron
and dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel."

10Now therefore, kings, be wise;
be warned, judges of the earth.

11Serve the LORD with fear,
and rejoice with trembling.

12Kiss the son, or he will be angry, and you will perish in the way,
for his anger is quickly kindled.
Blessed are all who take refuge in him.

Notes

  • v2 "His anointed" — meshicho, His messiah, the king anointed with oil (1 Samuel 16:13). The apostles read the psalm of Jesus: the kings of the earth set themselves… against the Lord and against His Anointed (Acts 4:25–27). The psalm itself is rendered as the Old Testament has it, with lowercase for the king; the New Testament quotations will capitalize.

  • v4 "the Lord" — Adonai, after He who sits in the heavens; God's laughter at the plots of kings (37:13; 59:8).

  • v6 "on Zion, My holy mountain" — the hill of Jerusalem where the king was enthroned and the temple stood.

  • v7 "You are My son; today I have fathered you" — the king becomes God's son on the day of his anointing: I will be to him a father, and he shall be to Me a son (2 Samuel 7:14). The voice from heaven at Jesus' baptism, You are My beloved Son (Mark 1:11), and Acts 13:33 and Hebrews 1:5; 5:5 take up these words.

  • v9 "break them with a rod of iron" — the Greek reads shepherd them with a rod of iron, from the same letters with other vowels, and Revelation 2:27; 12:5; 19:15 follow the Greek.

  • v12 "Kiss the son" — nashqu var: bar is the Aramaic word for son, where the Hebrew word is ben (v7). The kiss is the act of homage to a king (1 Samuel 10:1). The Greek reads take hold of instruction; others read kiss purely, or move the words: with trembling kiss his feet. Whether he in the rest of the verse is the LORD or the son is not certain.

  • v12 "Blessed are all who take refuge in him" — the psalm ends with the word that began Psalm 1, ashrei, blessed; the two psalms open the book together.

speech.text: Psalms 2
Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot in vain?
The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD and against His anointed:
"Let us burst their bonds apart and cast their cords away from us."
He who sits in the heavens laughs; the Lord holds them in derision.
Then He will speak to them in His anger and terrify them in His fury:
"As for Me, I have set My king on Zion, My holy mountain."
I will tell of the decree of the LORD. He said to me, "You are My son; today I have fathered you.
Ask of Me, and I will make the nations your inheritance, and the ends of the earth your possession.
You will break them with a rod of iron and dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel."
Now therefore, kings, be wise; be warned, judges of the earth.
Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
Kiss the son, or he will be angry, and you will perish in the way, for his anger is quickly kindled. Blessed are all who take refuge in him.

chapters.title: Salvation Belongs to the LORD
chapters.html:
Psalms 3

A psalm of David, when he fled from Absalom his son.

1LORD, how many are my foes!
Many are rising against me;

2many are saying of my soul,
"There is no salvation for him in God." Selah

3But You, LORD, are a shield around me,
my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.

4I cried aloud to the LORD,
and He answered me from His holy mountain. Selah

5I lay down and slept;
I woke again, for the LORD sustains me.

6I will not be afraid of the tens of thousands of people
who have set themselves against me all around.

7Arise, LORD!
Save me, my God!
For You strike all my enemies on the cheek;
You break the teeth of the wicked.

8Salvation belongs to the LORD;
Your blessing be on Your people! Selah

Notes

  • The title and the numbering — the Hebrew counts the title as verse 1, so the Hebrew numbers are one ahead of the English through the psalm.

  • The title "when he fled from Absalom his son" — the flight of David over the Mount of Olives (2 Samuel 15:13–30). It is the first psalm with a title, and the first linked to a moment in David's life.

  • v1 "how many are my foes!" — How many, rabbu… rabbim… rabbim, three times in two verses, as the conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing (2 Samuel 15:12).

  • v2 "Selah" — a word of uncertain meaning, found seventy-one times in the Psalms and three times in Habakkuk 3; perhaps a direction to the singers or players, a pause or a lifting up. It is kept as it stands, in italics, where the Hebrew puts it.

  • v2 "There is no salvation for him in God" — as Shimei cursed David on the road (2 Samuel 16:7–8).

  • v3 "the one who lifts up my head" — the fleeing king went up the Mount of Olives with his head covered (2 Samuel 15:30); God will lift it.

  • v5 "I lay down and slept" — the calm of a man who trusts God in the middle of a rebellion; In peace I will both lie down and sleep (4:8).

  • v7 "strike all my enemies on the cheek… break the teeth" — the enemy as a beast whose jaws are broken (58:6; Job 29:17).

  • v8 "Salvation belongs to the LORD" — la-YHWH ha-yeshu'ah, the answer to the taunt of v2; Salvation belongs to our God (Revelation 7:10).

speech.text: Psalms 3
LORD, how many are my foes! Many are rising against me;
many are saying of my soul, "There is no salvation for him in God." Selah
But You, LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.
I cried aloud to the LORD, and He answered me from His holy mountain. Selah
I lay down and slept; I woke again, for the LORD sustains me.
I will not be afraid of the tens of thousands of people who have set themselves against me all around.
Arise, LORD! Save me, my God! For You strike all my enemies on the cheek; You break the teeth of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to the LORD; Your blessing be on Your people! Selah

chapters.title: In Peace I Will Lie Down
chapters.html:
Psalms 4

For the director: with stringed instruments. A psalm of David.

1Answer me when I call, God of my righteousness!
You gave me room when I was in distress;
be gracious to me and hear my prayer.

2Sons of men, how long will my honor be turned to shame?
How long will you love emptiness and seek after lies? Selah

3Know that the LORD has set apart the faithful for Himself;
the LORD hears when I call to Him.

4Tremble, and do not sin;
speak in your hearts on your beds, and be silent. Selah

5Offer sacrifices of righteousness,
and trust in the LORD.

6Many are saying, "Who will show us good?"
Lift up the light of Your face on us, LORD.

7You have put joy in my heart,
more than when their grain and new wine abound.

8In peace I will both lie down and sleep,
for You alone, LORD, make me dwell in safety.

Notes

  • The title "For the director" — la-menatse'ach, found in fifty-five psalm titles and in Habakkuk 3:19: for the leader of the temple music. With stringed instruments is bi-neginot.

  • v1 "You gave me room when I was in distress" — ba-tsar hirchavta li: distress is a narrow place, and God sets the sufferer in a broad one (18:19; 118:5).

  • v2 "Sons of men" — benei ish, men of rank, perhaps those who slander the king; emptiness and lies may be false gods (40:4).

  • v3 "the faithful" — chasid, one who keeps chesed, loyal love, toward God.

  • v4 "Tremble, and do not sin" — rigzu, tremble with anger or with fear. The Greek has Be angry, and do not sin, which Paul quotes (Ephesians 4:26).

  • v6 "Lift up the light of Your face on us" — the priestly blessing, The LORD make His face shine on you (Numbers 6:25–26).

  • v7 "their grain and new wine" — the joy of harvest; God's gift of joy is greater than the harvest of those who ask Who will show us good?

  • v8 "In peace I will both lie down and sleep" — an evening psalm, as Psalm 3 is a morning psalm (3:5). Alone may go with You or with me: You make me dwell alone in safety (Deuteronomy 33:28).

speech.text: Psalms 4
Answer me when I call, God of my righteousness! You gave me room when I was in distress; be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
Sons of men, how long will my honor be turned to shame? How long will you love emptiness and seek after lies? Selah
Know that the LORD has set apart the faithful for Himself; the LORD hears when I call to Him.
Tremble, and do not sin; speak in your hearts on your beds, and be silent. Selah
Offer sacrifices of righteousness, and trust in the LORD.
Many are saying, "Who will show us good?" Lift up the light of Your face on us, LORD.
You have put joy in my heart, more than when their grain and new wine abound.
In peace I will both lie down and sleep, for You alone, LORD, make me dwell in safety.

chapters.title: In the Morning You Hear My Voice
chapters.html:
Psalms 5

For the director: for the flutes. A psalm of David.

1Listen to my words, LORD;
consider my sighing.

2Pay attention to the sound of my cry,
my King and my God,
for to You I pray.

3LORD, in the morning You hear my voice;
in the morning I set it out before You, and watch.

4For You are not a God who delights in wickedness;
evil cannot live as a guest with You.

5The boastful will not stand before Your eyes;
You hate all who do iniquity.

6You destroy those who speak lies;
the LORD abhors the man of bloodshed and deceit.

7But I, through the greatness of Your loyal love, will come into Your house;
I will bow down toward Your holy temple in fear of You.

8Lead me, LORD, in Your righteousness because of those who watch me;
make Your way straight before me.

9For there is nothing reliable in their mouth;
their inner part is ruin;
their throat is an open grave;
they make their tongue smooth.

10Hold them guilty, God;
let them fall by their own counsels;
for their many transgressions drive them out,
for they have rebelled against You.

11But let all who take refuge in You rejoice;
let them sing for joy forever,
and shelter them,
so that those who love Your name may exult in You.

12For You bless the righteous, LORD;
You surround him with favor as with a shield.

Notes

  • The title "for the flutes" — el ha-nechilot, a word found only here; perhaps wind instruments, or a tune.

  • v3 "in the morning I set it out before You" — e'erokh, the verb for laying out the wood and the offering on the altar (Leviticus 1:7–8) and for setting out a case in court (Job 23:4). The morning prayer is laid before God like the morning sacrifice.

  • v4 "evil cannot live as a guest with You" — lo yegurkha ra, from gur, as the word table has it: LORD, who shall live as a guest in Your tent? (15:1).

  • v6 "the LORD abhors" — yeta'ev, from the root of to'evah; the man of bloodshed is ish damim, as David himself was called (2 Samuel 16:7–8).

  • v7 "Your holy temple" — heikhal, the palace of the King, here the house of God, whether the tent or the temple.

  • v8 "those who watch me" — shorerai, enemies who lie in wait. The written form has hoshar, a spelling of the same verb make straight, as read.

  • v9 "their throat is an open grave" — quoted by Paul among the verses showing that none is righteous (Romans 3:13).

  • v12 "as with a shield" — tsinnah, the large shield that covers the whole body (1 Samuel 17:7).

speech.text: Psalms 5
Listen to my words, LORD; consider my sighing.
Pay attention to the sound of my cry, my King and my God, for to You I pray.
LORD, in the morning You hear my voice; in the morning I set it out before You, and watch.
For You are not a God who delights in wickedness; evil cannot live as a guest with You.
The boastful will not stand before Your eyes; You hate all who do iniquity.
You destroy those who speak lies; the LORD abhors the man of bloodshed and deceit.
But I, through the greatness of Your loyal love, will come into Your house; I will bow down toward Your holy temple in fear of You.
Lead me, LORD, in Your righteousness because of those who watch me; make Your way straight before me.
For there is nothing reliable in their mouth; their inner part is ruin; their throat is an open grave; they make their tongue smooth.
Hold them guilty, God; let them fall by their own counsels; for their many transgressions drive them out, for they have rebelled against You.
But let all who take refuge in You rejoice; let them sing for joy forever, and shelter them, so that those who love Your name may exult in You.
For You bless the righteous, LORD; You surround him with favor as with a shield.

chapters.title: Do Not Rebuke Me in Your Anger
chapters.html:
Psalms 6

For the director: with stringed instruments, on the eighth. A psalm of David.

1LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger,
nor discipline me in Your wrath.

2Be gracious to me, LORD, for I am fading away;
heal me, LORD, for my bones are shaken.

3My soul also is greatly shaken.
But You, LORD, how long?

4Turn, LORD, rescue my soul;
save me for the sake of Your loyal love.

5For in death there is no remembrance of You;
in Sheol who will praise You?

6I am weary with my sighing;
every night I make my bed swim;
I drench my couch with my tears.

7My eye wastes away with grief;
it grows old because of all my foes.

8Depart from me, all who do iniquity,
for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.

9The LORD has heard my plea;
the LORD accepts my prayer.

10All my enemies will be put to shame and greatly shaken;
they will turn back and be put to shame in a moment.

Notes

  • The title "on the eighth" — al ha-sheminit, perhaps an eight-stringed instrument, or the lower octave (1 Chronicles 15:21).

  • The psalm — the first of the seven psalms the Church has prayed as the penitential psalms (6, 32, 38, 51, 102, 130, 143).

  • v1 "do not rebuke me in Your anger" — the same words open Psalm 38. The psalmist does not ask to escape correction, but to be corrected without wrath (Jeremiah 10:24).

  • vv2–3, 10 "shaken" — nivhalu, three times: the bones, the soul, and at last the enemies. What the sufferer felt passes to those who troubled him.

  • v3 "But You, LORD, how long?" — the sentence breaks off. The written text has ve-at, a spelling of You.

  • v5 "in Sheol who will praise You?" — the dead do not praise God in the world below (30:9; 88:10–12; Isaiah 38:18).

  • v8 "Depart from me, all who do iniquity" — the words Jesus will say on the last day (Matthew 7:23; Luke 13:27).

  • v10 "turn back… in a moment" — yashuvu, turn back, the word the psalmist used to God in v4: when God turns, the enemies turn away.

speech.text: Psalms 6
LORD, do not rebuke me in Your anger, nor discipline me in Your wrath.
Be gracious to me, LORD, for I am fading away; heal me, LORD, for my bones are shaken.
My soul also is greatly shaken. But You, LORD, how long?
Turn, LORD, rescue my soul; save me for the sake of Your loyal love.
For in death there is no remembrance of You; in Sheol who will praise You?
I am weary with my sighing; every night I make my bed swim; I drench my couch with my tears.
My eye wastes away with grief; it grows old because of all my foes.
Depart from me, all who do iniquity, for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.
The LORD has heard my plea; the LORD accepts my prayer.
All my enemies will be put to shame and greatly shaken; they will turn back and be put to shame in a moment.

chapters.title: God Is a Righteous Judge
chapters.html:
Psalms 7

A Shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD concerning Cush, a Benjaminite.

1LORD my God, in You I take refuge;
save me from all who pursue me, and rescue me,

2or like a lion they will tear my soul,
dragging it away, with no one to rescue.

3LORD my God, if I have done this,
if there is injustice in my hands,

4if I have repaid with evil the one at peace with me,
or plundered my enemy without cause,

5let the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it,
and trample my life to the ground,
and lay my honor in the dust. Selah

6Arise, LORD, in Your anger;
lift Yourself up against the fury of my foes;
awake for me; You have commanded judgment.

7Let the assembly of the peoples gather around You,
and over it return on high.

8The LORD judges the peoples;
judge me, LORD, according to my righteousness
and according to the integrity that is in me.

9Let the evil of the wicked come to an end,
and establish the righteous,
You who test hearts and minds, righteous God.

10My shield is with God,
who saves the upright in heart.

11God is a righteous judge,
and a God who is angry every day.

12If a man does not turn back, He will sharpen His sword;
He has bent His bow and made it ready.

13He has prepared for him the weapons of death;
He makes His arrows into fiery shafts.

14The wicked man is in labor with iniquity;
he has conceived trouble and given birth to falsehood.

15He dug a pit and hollowed it out,
and fell into the hole he was making.

16His trouble returns on his own head,
and his violence comes down on his own skull.

17I will give thanks to the LORD for His righteousness,
and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.

Notes

  • The title "A Shiggaion of David… concerning Cush, a Benjaminite" — shiggayon, a word found only here and in Habakkuk 3:1, perhaps a wild or wandering song. Cush the Benjaminite is not otherwise known; he may be one of Saul's men, of Saul's tribe, who slandered David (1 Samuel 24:9; 26:19).

  • v2 "like a lion" — David the shepherd knew the lion that carries off a lamb (1 Samuel 17:34–35).

  • vv3–5 "if I have done this" — an oath of clearing, as Job's in Job 31: if I have…, let….

  • v4 "or plundered my enemy without cause" — va-achalletsah, which can also mean rescued: I who rescued my enemy without cause, as David spared Saul (1 Samuel 24:10–11).

  • v9 "You who test hearts and minds" — libbot u-khelayot, hearts and kidneys, the seat of thought and of feeling (Jeremiah 11:20; Revelation 2:23).

  • v11 "a God who is angry every day" — zo'em, indignant at wickedness; the Greek reads not bringing His anger every day.

  • v12 "If a man does not turn back" — the subject may be the wicked man, who will not repent, or God, who will not turn from His purpose.

  • v14 "in labor with iniquity… conceived trouble and given birth to falsehood" — the words of Job 15:35 and Isaiah 59:4.

  • vv15–16 "He dug a pit… and fell into the hole" — Whoever digs a pit will fall into it (Proverbs 26:27; Ecclesiastes 10:8).

  • v17 "the LORD Most High" — YHWH Elyon, the name of God that Melchizedek blessed (Genesis 14:18–22).

speech.text: Psalms 7
LORD my God, in You I take refuge; save me from all who pursue me, and rescue me,
or like a lion they will tear my soul, dragging it away, with no one to rescue.
LORD my God, if I have done this, if there is injustice in my hands,
if I have repaid with evil the one at peace with me, or plundered my enemy without cause,
let the enemy pursue my soul and overtake it, and trample my life to the ground, and lay my honor in the dust. Selah
Arise, LORD, in Your anger; lift Yourself up against the fury of my foes; awake for me; You have commanded judgment.
Let the assembly of the peoples gather around You, and over it return on high.
The LORD judges the peoples; judge me, LORD, according to my righteousness and according to the integrity that is in me.
Let the evil of the wicked come to an end, and establish the righteous, You who test hearts and minds, righteous God.
My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge, and a God who is angry every day.
If a man does not turn back, He will sharpen His sword; He has bent His bow and made it ready.
He has prepared for him the weapons of death; He makes His arrows into fiery shafts.
The wicked man is in labor with iniquity; he has conceived trouble and given birth to falsehood.
He dug a pit and hollowed it out, and fell into the hole he was making.
His trouble returns on his own head, and his violence comes down on his own skull.
I will give thanks to the LORD for His righteousness, and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.

chapters.title: What Is Man?
chapters.html:
Psalms 8

For the director: on the Gittith. A psalm of David.

1LORD, our Lord,
how majestic is Your name in all the earth!
You have set Your glory above the heavens.

2Out of the mouth of children and nursing infants
You have founded strength because of Your foes,
to silence the enemy and the avenger.

3When I look at Your heavens, the work of Your fingers,
the moon and the stars, which You have set in place,

4what is man, that You remember him,
and the son of man, that You visit him?

5Yet You have made him little less than God
and crown him with glory and honor.

6You make him ruler over the works of Your hands;
You have put all things under his feet,

7all sheep and oxen,
and also the beasts of the field,

8the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea,
whatever passes along the paths of the seas.

9LORD, our Lord,
how majestic is Your name in all the earth!

Notes

  • The title "on the Gittith" — al ha-gittit, perhaps an instrument or a tune from Gath (also Psalms 81 and 84).

  • v1 "LORD, our Lord" — YHWH adoneinu; the same words close the psalm (v9), framing all of it in praise of God's name.

  • v2 "Out of the mouth of children and nursing infants" — the Greek has You have prepared praise, which Jesus quotes when the children cry out in the temple (Matthew 21:16).

  • v3 "the work of Your fingers" — the heavens as God's handiwork, done as finely as with the fingers (Exodus 31:18; Isaiah 40:12).

  • v4 "what is man, that You remember him?" — enosh, man in his frailty; visit is paqad, to come to with care (Genesis 21:1). Job turns the words into a complaint (Job 7:17–18).

  • v5 "little less than God" — me-Elohim, which the Greek renders than the angels; Hebrews 2:6–9 quotes the Greek and applies the verses to Jesus.

  • vv6–8 "You make him ruler over the works of Your hands" — the charge of Genesis 1:26–28, let them have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the heavens. He has put all things under His feet (1 Corinthians 15:27; Ephesians 1:22).

  • vv4–6 and the pronouns — the psalm is rendered as the Old Testament has it, man and the son of man in lowercase; the New Testament quotations will capitalize where they apply the words to Jesus.

speech.text: Psalms 8
LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth! You have set Your glory above the heavens.
Out of the mouth of children and nursing infants You have founded strength because of Your foes, to silence the enemy and the avenger.
When I look at Your heavens, the work of Your fingers, the moon and the stars, which You have set in place,
what is man, that You remember him, and the son of man, that You visit him?
Yet You have made him little less than God and crown him with glory and honor.
You make him ruler over the works of Your hands; You have put all things under his feet,
all sheep and oxen, and also the beasts of the field,
the birds of the heavens and the fish of the sea, whatever passes along the paths of the seas.
LORD, our Lord, how majestic is Your name in all the earth!

chapters.title: The LORD Sits Enthroned Forever
chapters.html:
Psalms 9

For the director: on Muth-labben. A psalm of David.

1I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart;
I will tell of all Your wonders.

2I will be glad and exult in You;
I will sing praise to Your name, Most High.

3When my enemies turn back,
they stumble and perish before You.

4For You have upheld my right and my cause;
You sat on the throne, judging in righteousness.

5You have rebuked the nations; You have destroyed the wicked;
You have blotted out their name forever and ever.

6The enemy has come to an end in ruins forever;
You have uprooted their cities;
the very memory of them has perished.

7But the LORD sits enthroned forever;
He has set up His throne for judgment,

8and He will judge the world in righteousness;
He will judge the peoples with uprightness.

9The LORD will be a stronghold for the oppressed,
a stronghold in times of trouble.

10Those who know Your name put their trust in You,
for You, LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.

11Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion!
Tell among the peoples His deeds!

12For He who avenges blood remembers them;
He does not forget the cry of the afflicted.

13Be gracious to me, LORD!
See my affliction from those who hate me,
You who lift me up from the gates of death,

14so that I may tell of all Your praises
in the gates of the daughter of Zion
and rejoice in Your salvation.

15The nations have sunk in the pit they made;
in the net they hid, their own foot has been caught.

16The LORD has made Himself known; He has carried out judgment;
the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah

17The wicked will return to Sheol,
all the nations that forget God.

18For the needy will not always be forgotten,
nor the hope of the poor perish forever.

19Arise, LORD! Let not man prevail;
let the nations be judged before You!

20Put them in fear, LORD!
Let the nations know that they are only men! Selah

Notes

  • v1 and Psalm 10 — Psalms 9 and 10 are one poem in the Hebrew, an alphabetic acrostic whose lines begin with the letters of the alphabet in turn, broken in places; Psalm 10 has no title of its own. The Greek, and the Ethiopian Psalter with it, count the two as one psalm, so from Psalm 10 to Psalm 147 their numbers run one behind the Hebrew and English. The English numbering is followed here.

  • The title "on Muth-labben" — al mut labben, on the death of the son; perhaps the name of a tune.

  • v4 "my right and my cause" — mishpati ve-dini, the words of a law court. God sits as judge for the oppressed.

  • v12 "He who avenges blood" — doresh damim, He who requires blood, as God required Abel's blood (Genesis 4:10; 9:5).

  • vv12, 18 "the afflicted… the poor" — the written text has aniyyim, the afflicted, where the read form has anavim, the humble, and the reverse in v18; the two words are near in meaning, and the read form is followed.

  • v15 "the pit they made… their own foot has been caught" — the wicked caught in their own trap, as in 7:15–16.

  • v16 "Higgaion. Selah" — higgayon, murmuring, meditation, perhaps a musical direction (92:3), with Selah (3:2).

  • v17 "The wicked will return to Sheol" — return, as man returns to the dust (Genesis 3:19).

  • v20 "only men" — enosh, man in his frailty, as in 8:4.

speech.text: Psalms 9
I will give thanks to the LORD with my whole heart; I will tell of all Your wonders.
I will be glad and exult in You; I will sing praise to Your name, Most High.
When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish before You.
For You have upheld my right and my cause; You sat on the throne, judging in righteousness.
You have rebuked the nations; You have destroyed the wicked; You have blotted out their name forever and ever.
The enemy has come to an end in ruins forever; You have uprooted their cities; the very memory of them has perished.
But the LORD sits enthroned forever; He has set up His throne for judgment,
and He will judge the world in righteousness; He will judge the peoples with uprightness.
The LORD will be a stronghold for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.
Those who know Your name put their trust in You, for You, LORD, have not forsaken those who seek You.
Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion! Tell among the peoples His deeds!
For He who avenges blood remembers them; He does not forget the cry of the afflicted.
Be gracious to me, LORD! See my affliction from those who hate me, You who lift me up from the gates of death,
so that I may tell of all Your praises in the gates of the daughter of Zion and rejoice in Your salvation.
The nations have sunk in the pit they made; in the net they hid, their own foot has been caught.
The LORD has made Himself known; He has carried out judgment; the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgaion. Selah
The wicked will return to Sheol, all the nations that forget God.
For the needy will not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever.
Arise, LORD! Let not man prevail; let the nations be judged before You!
Put them in fear, LORD! Let the nations know that they are only men! Selah

chapters.title: Why Do You Stand Far Away?
chapters.html:
Psalms 10

1Why, LORD, do You stand far away?
Why do You hide Yourself in times of trouble?

2In arrogance the wicked hotly pursue the poor;
let them be caught in the schemes they have devised.

3For the wicked boasts of the desires of his soul,
and the greedy man curses and despises the LORD.

4The wicked, in the pride of his face, does not seek Him;
all his thoughts are, "There is no God."

5His ways prosper at all times;
Your judgments are on high, out of his sight;
as for all his foes, he snorts at them.

6He says in his heart, "I will not be moved;
through all generations I will not meet trouble."

7His mouth is full of cursing, deceit and oppression;
under his tongue are trouble and iniquity.

8He sits in ambush in the villages;
in hiding places he murders the innocent;
his eyes watch in secret for the helpless.

9He lies in wait in secret like a lion in his thicket;
he lies in wait to seize the poor;
he seizes the poor when he draws him into his net.

10The helpless is crushed, he sinks down,
and falls by his might.

11He says in his heart, "God has forgotten;
He has hidden His face; He will never see it."

12Arise, LORD; God, lift up Your hand;
do not forget the afflicted.

13Why does the wicked despise God
and say in his heart, "You will not require it"?

14But You do see, for You look on trouble and grief,
to take it into Your hand;
the helpless commits himself to You;
You have been the helper of the fatherless.

15Break the arm of the wicked and the evildoer;
seek out his wickedness until You find none.

16The LORD is King forever and ever;
the nations perish from His land.

17LORD, You hear the desire of the humble;
You strengthen their heart; You incline Your ear

18to do justice to the fatherless and the oppressed,
so that man, who is of the earth, may terrify no more.

Notes

  • The psalm — the second half of the acrostic begun in Psalm 9 (see the note there); it has no title.

  • v1 "Why, LORD, do You stand far away?" — the same words as 9:9, in times of trouble, now turned to complaint: the stronghold seems absent.

  • v3 "the greedy man curses and despises the LORD" — botsea berekh, blesses, the scribes' substitute for curses (as in Job 1:5). It can also be read the greedy man blesses himself.

  • v4 "There is no God" — the practical atheist, who lives as if God did not see (14:1; 53:1).

  • v7 "His mouth is full of cursing" — quoted by Paul in Romans 3:14.

  • vv8–10 — the wicked as a hunter and a lion lying in wait (17:12). The helpless, chel'kah, is a word found only in this psalm (vv8, 10, 14). In v10 the written text joins two words, chel ka'im, read as one, the helpless.

  • v13 "You will not require it" — lo tidrosh, God will not call him to account; the answer comes in v15, seek out, the same verb.

  • v14 "the helper of the fatherless" — a father of the fatherless… is God in His holy habitation (68:5; Deuteronomy 10:18).

  • v16 "The LORD is King forever and ever" — The LORD will reign forever and ever (Exodus 15:18).

  • v18 "man, who is of the earth" — enosh min ha-arets, frail man, made of earth, against God the King.

speech.text: Psalms 10
Why, LORD, do You stand far away? Why do You hide Yourself in times of trouble?

to do justice to the fatherless and the oppressed, so that man, who is of the earth, may terrify no more.

chapters.title: In the LORD I Take Refuge
chapters.html:
Psalms 11

For the director. Of David.

1In the LORD I take refuge;
how can you say to my soul,
"Flee like a bird to your mountain,

2for the wicked bend the bow;
they have set their arrow on the string
to shoot in the dark at the upright in heart;

3if the foundations are torn down,
what can the righteous do?"

4The LORD is in His holy temple;
the LORD, His throne is in heaven;
His eyes see, His eyelids test the children of man.

5The LORD tests the righteous,
but His soul hates the wicked and the one who loves violence.

6On the wicked He will rain coals,
fire and sulfur and a scorching wind
will be the portion of their cup.

7For the LORD is righteous; He loves righteous deeds;
the upright will see His face.

Notes

  • v1 and the title — here, as in Psalms 14 and 15, the short title shares the first verse with the opening words in the Hebrew, so the verse numbers of Hebrew and English agree.

  • v1 "Flee like a bird to your mountain" — the advice of friends who see no hope; the written text has the plural, flee (you all), the read form the singular, followed here.

  • v3 "if the foundations are torn down" — ha-shatot, the pillars of society, law and justice (82:5).

  • v4 "His eyelids test the children of man" — God looks closely, narrowing His eyes like one who examines (Proverbs 15:3).

  • v5 "The LORD tests the righteous" — the same verb as v4: the testing of the righteous is not hatred but refining (66:10; Job 23:10).

  • v6 "He will rain coals, fire and sulfur" — the Hebrew has pachim, snares; read with one vowel changed, pachamei, coals of, as the Greek has it. The fire and sulfur of Sodom (Genesis 19:24).

  • v6 "the portion of their cup" — the cup of God's wrath that the wicked must drink (75:8; Isaiah 51:17).

  • v7 "the upright will see His face" — the reward of the righteous, I will see Your face in righteousness (17:15; Matthew 5:8). It may also be read His face sees the upright.

speech.text: Psalms 11
In the LORD I take refuge; how can you say to my soul, "Flee like a bird to your mountain,
for the wicked bend the bow; they have set their arrow on the string to shoot in the dark at the upright in heart;
if the foundations are torn down, what can the righteous do?"
The LORD is in His holy temple; the LORD, His throne is in heaven; His eyes see, His eyelids test the children of man.
The LORD tests the righteous, but His soul hates the wicked and the one who loves violence.
On the wicked He will rain coals, fire and sulfur and a scorching wind will be the portion of their cup.
For the LORD is righteous; He loves righteous deeds; the upright will see His face.

chapters.title: The Words of the LORD Are Pure
chapters.html:
Psalms 12

For the director: on the eighth. A psalm of David.

1Save, LORD, for the faithful one is gone;
the trustworthy have vanished from among the children of man.

2Everyone speaks emptiness to his neighbor;
with smooth lips and a double heart they speak.

3May the LORD cut off all smooth lips,
the tongue that speaks great things,

4those who say, "With our tongue we will prevail;
our lips are our own; who is master over us?"

5"Because the poor are plundered, because the needy groan,
now I will arise," says the LORD;
"I will set him in the safety he longs for."

6The words of the LORD are pure words,
silver refined in a furnace in the earth,
purified seven times.

7You, LORD, will keep them;
You will guard him from this generation forever.

8On every side the wicked prowl,
when vileness is exalted among the children of man.

Notes

  • The title "on the eighth" — as in Psalm 6.

  • v1 "the faithful one is gone" — chasid, as in 4:3; The godly has perished from the earth (Micah 7:2).

  • v2 "a double heart" — lev va-lev, a heart and a heart, one thing said and another meant (1 Chronicles 12:33).

  • v4 "our lips are our own" — itanu, with us: no one rules their speech.

  • v5 "now I will arise," says the LORD — God answers in the middle of the psalm, as a prophet would bring His word (Isaiah 33:10).

  • v5 "the safety he longs for" — yafiach lo, which may also mean the one they puff at, the poor man his enemies sneer at (10:5).

  • v6 "silver refined… purified seven times" — God's words against the empty words of v2: every word of God proves true (Proverbs 30:5; 18:30).

  • v7 "You will keep them… guard him" — the plural is the poor of v5, the singular each one of them; the Greek reads us in both lines.

speech.text: Psalms 12
Save, LORD, for the faithful one is gone; the trustworthy have vanished from among the children of man.
Everyone speaks emptiness to his neighbor; with smooth lips and a double heart they speak.
May the LORD cut off all smooth lips, the tongue that speaks great things,
those who say, "With our tongue we will prevail; our lips are our own; who is master over us?"
"Because the poor are plundered, because the needy groan, now I will arise," says the LORD; "I will set him in the safety he longs for."
The words of the LORD are pure words, silver refined in a furnace in the earth, purified seven times.
You, LORD, will keep them; You will guard him from this generation forever.
On every side the wicked prowl, when vileness is exalted among the children of man.

chapters.title: How Long, LORD?
chapters.html:
Psalms 13

For the director. A psalm of David.

1How long, LORD? Will You forget me forever?
How long will You hide Your face from me?

2How long must I take counsel in my soul,
with sorrow in my heart all the day?
How long will my enemy be exalted over me?

3Look on me and answer me, LORD my God;
light up my eyes, or I will sleep the sleep of death,

4and my enemy will say, "I have overcome him,"
and my foes will rejoice because I am shaken.

5But I have trusted in Your loyal love;
my heart will rejoice in Your salvation.

6I will sing to the LORD,
because He has dealt bountifully with me.

Notes

  • vv1–2 "How long?" — ad anah, four times: the cry of the lament psalms (6:3; 74:10; 89:46). The psalm moves in three steps, from complaint (vv1–2) to prayer (vv3–4) to trust (vv5–6).

  • v1 "Will You forget me forever?" — the opposite of He does not forget the cry of the afflicted (9:12); the sufferer feels what faith denies.

  • v3 "light up my eyes" — give me life and strength again (1 Samuel 14:27, 29; Ezra 9:8); dim eyes are a sign of death.

  • v3 "or I will sleep the sleep of death" — death as a sleep from which there is no waking (Jeremiah 51:39); the fear runs on into v4, where the enemy would boast over him.

  • v5 "Your loyal love" — chesed, the ground of trust when God seems far.

  • v6 "He has dealt bountifully with me" — gamal alai, the past tense of faith: the psalmist sings as though the answer had already come. The Greek adds a line, and I will sing to the name of the Lord Most High, from 7:17.

speech.text: Psalms 13
How long, LORD? Will You forget me forever? How long will You hide Your face from me?
How long must I take counsel in my soul, with sorrow in my heart all the day? How long will my enemy be exalted over me?
Look on me and answer me, LORD my God; light up my eyes, or I will sleep the sleep of death,
and my enemy will say, "I have overcome him," and my foes will rejoice because I am shaken.
But I have trusted in Your loyal love; my heart will rejoice in Your salvation.
I will sing to the LORD, because He has dealt bountifully with me.

chapters.title: The Fool Says in His Heart
chapters.html:
Psalms 14

For the director. Of David.

1The fool says in his heart, "There is no God."
They are corrupt; they do detestable deeds;
there is no one who does good.

2The LORD looks down from heaven on the children of man,
to see if there is anyone who understands,
who seeks God.

3They have all turned aside; together they have become corrupt;
there is no one who does good,
not even one.

4Do they have no knowledge, all who do iniquity,
who eat up my people as they eat bread,
and do not call on the LORD?

5There they are in great terror,
for God is with the generation of the righteous.

6You would put to shame the counsel of the poor,
but the LORD is his refuge.

7Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion!
When the LORD restores the fortunes of His people,
let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

Notes

  • The psalm — repeated almost word for word as Psalm 53, which uses God (Elohim) where this psalm has the LORD, and differs in vv5–6.

  • v1 "The fool says in his heart" — naval, not a man without intelligence but a man without reverence, like Nabal (1 Samuel 25:25). There is no God is the claim of 10:4: God does not see, and does not act.

  • v1 "they do detestable deeds" — hit'ivu, from the root of to'evah, as the word table has it.

  • v2 "The LORD looks down from heaven" — as He came down to see the tower of Babel (Genesis 11:5) and Sodom (Genesis 18:21).

  • vv1–3 "there is no one who does good, not even one" — Paul gathers these lines with others into one charge, None is righteous, no, not one (Romans 3:10–12). The Greek of the psalm adds after v3 the lines Paul goes on to quote in Romans 3:13–18; they come from Psalms 5, 140, 10 and 36 and Isaiah 59, and are not in the Hebrew here.

  • v4 "who eat up my people as they eat bread" — they devour the poor as casually as they eat a meal (Micah 3:3).

  • v6 "the counsel of the poor" — atsat ani, the plans and hopes of the poor man, which the wicked mock.

  • v7 "When the LORD restores the fortunes of His people" — be-shuv YHWH shevut ammo, the words of the end of Job (Job 42:10).

speech.text: Psalms 14
The fool says in his heart, "There is no God." They are corrupt; they do detestable deeds; there is no one who does good.
The LORD looks down from heaven on the children of man, to see if there is anyone who understands, who seeks God.
They have all turned aside; together they have become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
Do they have no knowledge, all who do iniquity, who eat up my people as they eat bread, and do not call on the LORD?
There they are in great terror, for God is with the generation of the righteous.
You would put to shame the counsel of the poor, but the LORD is his refuge.
Oh that the salvation of Israel would come out of Zion! When the LORD restores the fortunes of His people, let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad.

chapters.title: Who Shall Live as a Guest in Your Tent?
chapters.html:
Psalms 15

A psalm of David.

1LORD, who shall live as a guest in Your tent?
Who shall dwell on Your holy mountain?

2The one who walks blamelessly and does what is right
and speaks truth in his heart;

3who does not slander with his tongue,
does no evil to his neighbor,
nor takes up a reproach against his friend;

4in whose eyes a vile person is despised,
but who honors those who fear the LORD;
who swears to his own hurt and does not change;

5who does not lend his money at interest,
nor take a bribe against the innocent.
The one who does these things will never be moved.

Notes

  • v1 "who shall live as a guest in Your tent?" — yagur, from gur, as the word table has it: even the righteous are guests in God's house, received by His welcome (5:4; 39:12). The question was asked at the gate of the temple, and the answer is given in ten marks of the righteous (compare 24:3–6; Isaiah 33:14–16).

  • v2 "walks blamelessly" — tamim, whole, of one piece, the word for Noah and Job (Genesis 6:9; Job 1:1).

  • v2 "speaks truth in his heart" — his inner words and his outer words agree, the opposite of the double heart of 12:2.

  • v4 "who swears to his own hurt and does not change" — he keeps his oath even when it costs him (Leviticus 5:4; Judges 11:35).

  • v5 "who does not lend his money at interest" — neshekh, bite, interest charged to a fellow Israelite in need, forbidden by the law (Exodus 22:25; Leviticus 25:36–37; Deuteronomy 23:19).

  • v5 "nor take a bribe against the innocent" — You shall not take a bribe (Exodus 23:8; Deuteronomy 16:19).

  • v5 "will never be moved" — against the wicked man who boasts I will not be moved (10:6): only the righteous truly stands.

speech.text: Psalms 15
LORD, who shall live as a guest in Your tent? Who shall dwell on Your holy mountain?
The one who walks blamelessly and does what is right and speaks truth in his heart;
who does not slander with his tongue, does no evil to his neighbor, nor takes up a reproach against his friend;
in whose eyes a vile person is despised, but who honors those who fear the LORD; who swears to his own hurt and does not change;
who does not lend his money at interest, nor take a bribe against the innocent. The one who does these things will never be moved.
